cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the UX Conversational Designer position at AMA, supporting your telecom client's Digital Factory team. Although my title has been in digital marketing and SEO, my work sits at the intersection of language, technology, and user experience—exactly where conversational design lives. I have spent the last years designing digital experiences that are clear, empathetic, and measurable, and I am eager to focus that skillset on conversational interfaces.

In my current role at Episto, I handle on-page SEO and content for client websites, but I also use AI tools daily to research, write, and audit. I have built AI agents and MCP integrations that automate workflows, giving me a practical understanding of how NLP and AI-powered assistants function. At Knowledge Experts, I built and optimized websites, including mirook.com, where I implemented JSON-LD schema, knowledge-graph markup, and an llms.txt file. This required translating technical logic into user-friendly structures—a core skill for conversational design. I also ran iterative audits that improved search health, mirroring the KPI-driven optimization you seek.

While I have not held the title of Conversational Designer, I have designed multi-turn interactions through content strategy and user research. My front-end development background (AngularJS, JavaScript) helps me assess the feasibility and limitations of conversational solutions. I am fluent in English, native in Turkish, and have working knowledge of Dutch, which supports inclusive, multilingual design.

I am passionate about language, AI, and creating conversations that feel natural and helpful. I would welcome the chance to bring my mix of UX, content, and technical skills to your multidisciplinary squad, and to learn from your NLP and AI/ML specialists. Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,
Baver Ok
